tasks.title: Forge scopes, authorization order, target selection and route skeleton
steps: Write TS-30-4,5,6,8,9,13,14 in internal/forge (testhelpers_test.go with an X-Test-Auth middleware calling apikit.SetAuthInfo, a minimal workspaces table created like internal/carrypatch/testhelpers_test.go createWorkspacesTable, a counting forge stub and counting resolver/variable closures) and confirm they fail
permissions.go: `ForgeReadScope`/`ForgeWriteScope` as apikit.Permission{Resource:"forge",Action:"read"|"write"} and `Permissions()` returning exactly [read, write]

auth.go: standalone isAdmin/isAPIKey/isPAT/hasScope/canReadForge/canWriteForge taking *apikit.AuthInfo, copied from internal/sandboxes/auth.go; forge:write implies forge:read; unknown credential types get false

config.go: `Config{DB *sql.DB; ResolveOriginAuth, ResolveUpstreamAuth func(slug string)(transport.AuthMethod,error); GetVariable func(ownerType, ownerID, key string)(string,error); Transport http.RoundTripper; NewClient func(issuex.Options)(issuex.Client,error)}`

routes.go: `RegisterRoutes(api *echo.Group, cfg Config)` registering the ten GET routes under /workspaces/:slug (/forge, /forge/repository, /issues, /issues/:n, /issues/:n/comments, /pulls/:n, /pulls/:n/state, /pulls/:n/files, /pulls/:n/checks, /pulls/:n/reviews)

Implement `authorize(c)` in order: nil auth -> 401; missing scope -> 403 with message 'PAT requires forge:read scope'; wsaccess.AuthorizeWorkspace -> 404; then a `loadRemotes` SELECT of git_url, workspace_mode, upstream_url (NULL mode treated as standard, NULL upstream as empty)

Implement target parsing (absent/origin -> origin; upstream only when carry_patch with non-empty upstream_url else 400 error_type workspace_mode_mismatch; anything else including empty -> 400 listing 'origin' and 'upstream'); GET /forge does not take target
After authorize and target, route handlers answer a temporary 501 via apikit.WriteAPIError; tasks 3-5 replace it with the real operation

Wire cmd/af-hub/main.go: `extraPerms = append(extraPerms, forge.Permissions()...)` before MountWorkspaceHandlers, and `forge.RegisterRoutes(server.APIGroup(), forge.Config{...})` after it with closures around workspace.ResolveCloneAuth(store, slug) and workspace.ResolveUpstreamAuthMethod(store, slug) and store.GetVariableValue
done_when: `go build ./cmd/af-hub` succeeds with forge routes mounted

tasks.title: Build a fresh issuex client per request and serve GET /forge/repository
steps: Write TS-30-11,12,15,16,17,18,19,20 (TLS httptest stubs with Config.Transport = ts.Client().Transport, a fake NewClient factory capturing issuex.Options for TS-30-19, a real secrets store for TS-30-15) and confirm they fail

client.go: `buildClient(ctx, slug, target, remote)` returning the issuex client, the credential kind and the resolved token; origin uses ResolveOriginAuth + FORGE_API_URL, upstream uses ResolveUpstreamAuth + UPSTREAM_FORGE_API_URL with no fallback to FORGE_API_URL
Read the variable through GetVariable("workspace", slug, NAME): *secrets.NotFoundError means unset, any other error is a 500 (logged without secret values); resolver errors likewise 500
Validate a set API URL (absolute https with host, no userinfo, query or fragment) else 422 error_type forge_api_url_invalid whose message names the variable and rule but not the value
Credential kind from the resolver result: *githttp.BasicAuth with Username x-token-auth -> pat, other username -> basic (password is the token), nil -> none (empty token)

Parse the repo with issuex.ParseRemote(remote); failure -> 422 forge_unknown naming the URL with userinfo stripped; issuex.ErrAmbiguousForge from NewWithOptions (errors.Is) -> 422 forge_unknown naming host and FORGE_API_URL or UPSTREAM_FORGE_API_URL; nothing is cached between calls

Create the process-wide http.Client in Config setup using Config.Transport or http.DefaultTransport.Clone() (hardening comes in task 7); call NewClient (default issuex.NewWithOptions) with Options{BaseURL, Token, RemoteURL, Repo, HTTPClient}
errors.go: single `writeForgeError(c, ...)` entry point handling the construction errors here (400/422/500); the issuex-error mapping is added in task 6
Replace the 501 placeholder of GET /forge/repository with a call to GetRepository and JSON-encode the result; other routes remain placeholders

tasks.title: Implement the remaining read routes with parameter validation
steps: Write TS-30-7,10,32,33,34,35,36,37 (TS-30-32 uses a TLS stub serving minimal GitHub JSON and compares with a direct real issuex client; TS-30-33/36 use a fake issuex.Client through Config.NewClient) and confirm they fail
Parse `:n` as a positive decimal integer (strconv, reject sign/dot/letters) and answer 400 naming parameter n before any client is built

Parse GET /issues query: state open|closed|all, sort created|updated, direction asc|desc, limit 1..100 default 30 (always passed), labels split on commas dropping empty items, assignee free text; absent parameters are not passed to issuex; 400 names the offending parameter

Implement handlers for /issues, /issues/:n (ReadIssue: issue, comments, truncation flag), /issues/:n/comments, /pulls/:n, /pulls/:n/state, /pulls/:n/files, /pulls/:n/checks, /pulls/:n/reviews calling ListIssues, ReadIssue, ListComments, ReadPullRequest, GetPRState, ReadChangedFiles, GetCIChecks, GetPRReviews
Encode results as issuex types unchanged; normalise nil slices to empty so list routes emit `[]` never `null`
Emit no audit event from any read handler (no audit import)
Confirm reads work on archived and clone_status-pending workspaces and never take wslock
done_when: all nine read routes return 200 against the stub

tasks.title: Implement GET /workspaces/:slug/forge diagnostic
steps: Write TS-30-26..31 (TS-30-26/28 use a counting transport asserting zero requests; TS-30-31 is a property test with generated tokens/usernames/passwords via testing/quick or a table of generated strings) and confirm they fail

Add a `describeRemote` helper in client.go that, without sending a request, validates the API URL variable (422 forge_api_url_invalid), parses the repo, classifies the forge via the issuex client's forge-kind/API-URL accessor (read aflib/issuex source in ../aflib to find the real accessor name and the repo type fields) and reports forge github|gitlab|unknown

Fill `upstream` with the same four fields from upstream_url, the upstream resolver and UPSTREAM_FORGE_API_URL on a carry_patch workspace with non-empty upstream_url, else null
Replace the GET /forge placeholder with the handler returning {forge, api_url, repository, credential, upstream}
done_when: GET /forge never makes an outbound request in any test

tasks.title: Map issuex and transport failures to hub errors with scrubbing and logging
steps: Write TS-30-38..47 (TLS stubs for each status class; TS-30-45 property test of the scrub function; TS-30-46/47 capture the log output via log.SetOutput or the package logger) and confirm they fail

scrub.go: copy the userinfo pattern `(?i)([a-z][a-z0-9+.\-]*://)[^/\s?#]*@` from internal/sandboxes/scrub.go; implement scrub(msg, token) = replace token with [redacted], strip URL userinfo (repeat passes), cut to 1024 bytes on a UTF-8 boundary, ensuring the token cannot reappear after the cut

Inspect ../aflib/issuex for its HTTP error type (status, message, retry-after) and rate-limit signal; use errors.As/errors.Is in a single mapForgeError(err, credKind, token) table: 404 -> 404 forge_not_found; 401 -> 502 forge_unauthenticated (+ hint naming GIT_PAT and GIT_PASSWORD when credential is basic); 403 non-rate-limit -> 502 forge_forbidden; rate limit -> 429 forge_rate_limited with Retry-After whole seconds rounded up (math.Ceil) only when known; other 4xx -> 422 forge_rejected; 5xx or unreadable response -> 502 forge_error
Map net/DNS/TCP/TLS errors (net.Error, *url.Error, x509 errors) to 502 forge_unreachable and context.DeadlineExceeded to 504 forge_timeout; a redirect-refusal error to 502 forge_error
Run every message through scrub; also scrub the userinfo from logged text
Log exactly one line per 5xx/429 answer with slug, target, operation (e.g. ListIssues) and forge status, never token, request body or response body
Route every handler's issuex error through mapForgeError via the one writeForgeError entry point

tasks.title: Harden the shared forge HTTP client: user agent, redirect policy and deadline
steps: Write TS-30-21 (property: generated bearer strings, headers and bodies), 22, 23 (set apikit.Version to 1.2.3 and restore), 24 (two TLS stubs on different hosts/ports) and 25 and confirm they fail
httpclient.go: build one *http.Client per process (sync.Once or built in RegisterRoutes) with base transport Config.Transport or http.DefaultTransport.Clone()
Wrap the transport in a round-tripper that clones the request and sets `User-Agent: af-hub/<apikit.Version>` read at request time, overriding any existing value
Set CheckRedirect to return an error when the redirect target host differs from the original request host; the mapper turns it into 502 forge_error
Use a package-level `callDeadline = 30 * time.Second` variable (test hook) and wrap each forge call in context.WithTimeout derived from the request context; deadline expiry maps to 504 forge_timeout
Never copy the incoming Authorization header or body into outbound requests; only the workspace token is sent
